chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Joe Smith as an all-around trumpeter
summary: Briggs judges Joe Smith a fine tone player with a half vibrato who could have been an excellent lead player but preferred hot playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Let me ask you while we're on the subject of trumpet players now, what about Joe Smith, I mean he was a pretty good reader and a pretty good lead player, or just a hot player?
Joe Smith was what you would call an all around trumpet player, more or less.
More or less, yes. But I think Al was more or less. I say all around, because I think my courses were not so bad --
And if I had to, I was on the spot, and I had to -- I had the responsibility, I think I would be in a position to take good care of him. And Joe
Smith should be a fine trumpet -- first trumpet player. He could have been, if he wanted to be.
But he wanted to be a hot player, mostly.
Yeh, he wanted to be hot player mostly. But that beautiful tone he had, 'cause he had a nice tone.
He had a half vibrato, which is very embellishing and everything else, and he could have been a real fine first trumpet player, if he wanted both. I mean, what you call "all around".
